objectives: Students should use cumulative frequency graphs to determine how many data values fall below or above certain thresholds (Maths 6.1)
Students should interpret cumulative frequency graphs to compare distributions (Maths 6.1)
Students should estimate the median, quartiles, and interquartile range from cumulative frequency graphs (Maths 6.1)

keyConcepts.explanation: A running total of frequencies, showing the number of data points less than or equal to a particular value.
The middle value in an ordered set of data, estimated from a cumulative frequency graph by finding the data value corresponding to half the total frequency.
The range between the lower quartile (25th percentile) and upper quartile (75th percentile), representing the middle 50% of the data.

steps.title: Introduction to Cumulative Frequency Graphs
steps.content: In this lesson, we explore how to use cumulative frequency graphs to find the number of data values above or below certain points, compare different datasets, and estimate key statistics such as median, quartiles, and interquartile range.

steps.title: Multiple Choice Question: Understanding Cumulative Frequency
steps.content: What does a point on a cumulative frequency graph represent?

questions.question: A point on a cumulative frequency graph shows:
options: The frequency of a single data value
The total number of data values less than or equal to a certain value
questions.answer: The total number of data values less than or equal to a certain value
questions.explanation: Each point on the cumulative frequency graph shows the cumulative number of data points up to that value.

steps.title: Dropdown Cloze: Estimating Median and Quartiles
steps.content: Fill in the blanks to complete the method for estimating the median and quartiles from a cumulative frequency graph.

questions.text: To estimate the median, find the value on the vertical axis that is ___1___ of the total frequency, then draw a horizontal line to the curve, and drop a vertical line down to the ___2___. For quartiles, do the same but use ___3___ and ___4___ of the total frequency.
questions.explanation: The median corresponds to half the total frequency; the lower and upper quartiles correspond to one quarter and three quarters respectively.

steps.title: Summary: Key Points on Cumulative Frequency Graphs
steps.content: Complete the summary by selecting the correct terms to fill the blanks:

questions.text: A cumulative frequency graph helps us find the ___1___ frequency up to a value. The ___2___ is found at half the total frequency, while the interquartile range is the difference between the ___3___ and ___4___.
questions.explanation: These terms are fundamental when interpreting cumulative frequency graphs.

steps.title: Practice Question: Using a Cumulative Frequency Graph
steps.content: Given a cumulative frequency graph with a total frequency of 80, estimate the median, lower quartile, upper quartile, and interquartile range.

subQuestions.question: Estimate the median value.
subQuestions.answer: The value corresponding to 40 on the vertical axis.

subQuestions.question: Estimate the lower quartile value.
subQuestions.answer: The value corresponding to 20 on the vertical axis.

subQuestions.question: Estimate the upper quartile value.
subQuestions.answer: The value corresponding to 60 on the vertical axis.

subQuestions.question: Calculate the interquartile range.
subQuestions.answer: Upper quartile value minus lower quartile value.

questions.explanation: Use half the total frequency for median, one quarter for lower quartile, and three quarters for upper quartile to make estimations from the graph.
